archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield-leaning)
archetype.definition: A 15th-year rhythm thrower who wins from the pocket on timing and decisiveness, now pushing the ball downfield more than he did at his peak and getting rid of it before sacks happen.

report.headline: A 38-year-old rebound built on deep shots, padded by red-zone TD luck.
report.take:
Cousins came into 2026 off what looked like the start of the end: in 2025 his YPA (6.4) ranked 40th and his CPOE (-2.8) 45th. Six games into his Raiders tenure he has bounced back to something close to his Minnesota prime. His EPA per dropback of 0.207 is far above the league's 0.034, his YPA is up 1.03 on last year, and his bad-throw rate is down 2.2 points. This is a real recovery in production, not a fluke week or two. The passing EPA climbed almost every week after a flat Week 1, through a stretch that included the Chiefs (3rd-ranked defense today) and the Chargers (9th).

The engine is downfield, which isn't the version of Cousins most people remember. On 25 throws of 20+ air yards he is at 0.946 EPA per attempt with a +9.4 CPOE, four touchdowns and no picks. His throws of 10+ air yards add up to 41.4 EPA, more than his entire dropback total, because the short game and the screens behind the line (-0.271 per play) give some of it back. His aggressiveness (18.78%) sits near the top of his career range. Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Cody White are all producing around half a point of EPA per target. The other half of his game is sack avoidance: his pressure-to-sack rate ranks 4th, and that's behind a line ranking 25th in hit rate allowed. He is beating pressure by getting the ball out, not by moving. He has -2 rushing yards, and his designed runs and scrambles are a non-factor.

Two things in the box score flatter him. First, the touchdowns. Fourteen leads the league, but 11 came in the red zone on just 36 attempts at a 50% completion rate and a 0.378 success rate, and his 6.6% TD rate is well above the league's 4.5%. The last three games (4.1%) already show it coming back down. Second, the accuracy is ordinary. His CPOE ranks 26th, and between 10 and 19 yards he completes 51.1% at -6.1 CPOE, with four of his five interceptions there. Over the last three games his CPOE is -4.1, including -9.7 against Buffalo, as his volume has risen to 40.3 attempts a game.

The 0-3 skid isn't on him. His EPA per dropback in those games (0.246) is higher than his season mark. He's losing because the Raiders' pass defense ranks 25th, their short-pass defense ranks last, and their run game ranks 29th, so every week turns into a shootout he has to win throwing. That role keeps the yardage steady and high. The touchdown pace will not hold, and the intermediate middle of the field is where the turnovers will keep coming from.

strengths.title: Deep ball is driving everything
strengths.body: His 20+ air-yard throws are the most efficient part of his game by a wide margin: efficient per attempt, accurate over expectation, and so far turnover-free. It comes from an aggressiveness rate above his Vikings-era norms and receivers who are winning down the field. The 25-attempt sample is small, so expect the per-throw figure to cool, but the willingness to throw deep looks like a real change in approach.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks behind a leaky line
strengths.body: His line ranks 25th in hit rate allowed, yet he is taking sacks on only 3.6% of dropbacks, 4th-best among qualifiers. He turns pressure into throws rather than sacks. That fits a career-long pattern of decisive pocket play, and this year's mark is better than any of his recent seasons, so some of it may settle back, but the trait is real.

strengths.title: An efficient target tree
strengths.body: Bowers (43 targets), Tucker and White are all producing roughly half a point of EPA per target. That gives him reliable answers both at tight end and outside, which keeps the offense's passing EPA 5th in the league despite a broken run game. The weak link is the volume going to Ashton Jeanty, whose targets are barely above zero EPA.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate built to regress
concerns.body: Eleven of his 14 touchdowns came in the red zone, where he completes only half his throws and succeeds on fewer than four in ten plays. That is a TD conversion rate the underlying efficiency doesn't support. The last three games' TD rate is already well below his season mark. Expect closer to two scores a game than the 40-TD pace.

concerns.title: Intermediate and middle-field misses
concerns.body: At 10-19 air yards he completes 51.1% at -6.1 CPOE, and four of his five interceptions came there. Throws over the middle carry a -10.4 CPOE. This window has been a weak spot through most of his career, and with the extra aggressiveness it is where turnover risk concentrates. It's a real flaw, not noise.

concerns.title: Accuracy slipping as volume rises
concerns.body: Over the last three games his CPOE fell to -4.1, bottoming out at -9.7 against Buffalo, while his attempts climbed past 40 a game. That is largely the cost of his situation: a pass defense ranked 25th forces him to chase shootouts. At 38 and coming off a weak 2025, it is still worth watching whether the heavy load wears on his ball placement.

trend.note: His passing EPA climbed almost every week after a flat Week 1 and peaked against Buffalo, with last-three efficiency above his season mark despite an 0-3 record. The caveat is a falling CPOE and touchdown rate, so the production is rising on volume and big plays rather than accuracy.

nextGame.headline: Clean pocket, closed deep lane: volume over fireworks against the Rams.
nextGame.body:
The Rams take away exactly what has powered his season. Their deep-pass defense is the stingiest in the league, they rank 8th in explosive pass rate allowed, and they have given up the 2nd-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks. They have also been the league's best defense against opposing top tight ends, which points straight at Bowers. The opening is underneath and to secondary receivers: offenses' third wideouts have run 5.2 PPR points a game over their averages against them. A Cousins who stays patient and attacks the short and intermediate areas can still move the ball. A Cousins who forces shots downfield is playing into their strength. As 4.5-point home underdogs with a 47.5 total, the Raiders project to trail, which keeps his attempts high.

Availability tilts the line of scrimmage his way. The Rams already ranked 30th in hit rate and 28th in sack rate. Myles Garrett remains on IR with no practice window opened, Kobie Turner is expected to land on IR, and Poona Ford is done for the year. Trent McDuffie sat last week with a groin injury and is listed out. If he misses again, their secondary loses its top corner and the cleaner pocket matters more. On the Raiders' side, Dont'e Thornton Jr. and Carter Runyon both carry IR return dates of this game but haven't played this year, so Thornton's activation would be a bonus rather than something to count on. The Rams lose Davante Adams and their kicker, which could slow the scoring pace on their end.

keyMatchups.title: League's best deep defense vs. his edge
keyMatchups.body: His season rests on 20+ yard throws, and no defense has been better at stopping them. Expect fewer shot plays to land and his yards per attempt to come down. Volume will have to make up the difference.

keyMatchups.title: A gutted Rams pass rush
keyMatchups.body: The Rams were already near the bottom in hits and sacks, and they are now without Garrett, Turner and Ford. That should give him the cleanest pockets he has seen since Week 1. His worst accuracy game came against Kansas City when he was pressured over a third of the time.

keyMatchups.title: Bowers blanketed, third options open
keyMatchups.body: Opposing top tight ends have been held to negative EPA per target by this defense. Third receivers, meanwhile, have feasted. How readily he moves off Bowers toward Tucker, White or a third option decides his efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Whether he takes the underneath and third-receiver looks or keeps forcing the intermediate middle against a defense that won't give up the deep ball.

restOfSeason.body:
The role is stable and favorable for volume. He is the unchallenged starter, he gets rid of the ball before sacks, and a defense this porous will keep him throwing 35-40 times a week. Yards are the most bankable part of his line, and roughly 250-290 a game is a fair expectation. The touchdowns are the piece to fade. Red-zone conversion at this rate on half-completion accuracy doesn't last, and his recent games already show it, so think 1.6-2.1 a game rather than the league-leading pace.

The deep-ball efficiency should cool from its current level but stay a genuine strength given his aggressiveness and receivers. The intermediate interceptions are a long-standing trait and will keep showing up. Fantasy-wise he stays a mid-pack QB1/QB2 type on passing alone. With no rushing floor, his weekly value swings on whether the downfield shots land.

confidence.note: Six games and a 25-attempt deep sample; role and volume are stable, and a long career gives a baseline.
